content: Cefdinir capsules should be used exclusively for the treatment or prevention of infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by bacteria susceptible to this antibiotic. This approach is essential to minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the effectiveness of cefdinir and other antibacterial agents. When available, culture and susceptibility data should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns may inform empirical therapy decisions. Cefdinir capsules are indicated for the treatment of mild to moderate infections caused by susceptible strains of designated microorganisms in the following conditions: Adults and Adolescents: 1. Community-Acquired Pneumonia: Caused by Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Haemophilus parainfluenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (penicillin-susceptible strains only), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). 2. Acute Exacerbations of Chronic Bronchitis: Caused by Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Haemophilus parainfluenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (penicillin-susceptible strains only), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). 3. Acute Maxillary Sinusitis: Caused by Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (penicillin-susceptible strains only), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). 4. Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis: Caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. Cefdinir is effective in eradicating S. pyogenes from the oropharynx. However, it has not been studied for the prevention of rheumatic fever following S. pyogenes pharyngitis/tonsillitis. Only intramuscular penicillin has been demonstrated to prevent rheumatic fever. 5. Uncomplicated Skin and Skin Structure Infections: Caused by Staphylococcus aureus (including beta-lactamase-producing strains) and Streptococcus pyogenes. Pediatric Patients: 1. Acute Bacterial Otitis Media: Caused by Haemophilus influenzae (including beta-lactamase-producing strains), Streptococcus pneumoniae (penicillin-susceptible strains only), and Moraxella catarrhalis (including beta-lactamase-producing strains). 2. Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis: Caused by Streptococcus pyogenes. Cefdinir is effective in eradicating S. pyogenes from the oropharynx. However, it has not been studied for the prevention of rheumatic fever following S. pyogenes pharyngitis/tonsillitis. Only intramuscular penicillin has been demonstrated to prevent rheumatic fever. 3. Uncomplicated Skin and Skin Structure Infections: Caused by Staphylococcus aureus (including beta-lactamase-producing strains) and Streptococcus pyogenes.
